summary: This component fetches and displays comments from Bluesky (a social media platform) on a blog post. It pulls the thread of replies for a specific post using the Bluesky API, filters out blocked users, flattens the reply tree into a single list with depth information for indentation, and renders each comment with the author's info, text with proper link handling, embedded media, and engagement metrics.

explanations.14: Bluesky uses byte offsets (counting individual bytes in UTF-8 encoding) rather than JavaScript's string character indices, which matters for emoji and accented characters—they take multiple bytes but count as one character in JS.
explanations.21: TextEncoder converts the post text string into raw UTF-8 bytes so we can slice it using Bluesky's byte offsets instead of character indices.
explanations.28: The function loops through each facet (rich-text feature like links or formatting) and reconstructs the post text piece by piece, inserting React elements where needed.
explanations.35: We search through the facet's features array to find a link—facets can contain multiple types of formatting applied to the same text span.
explanations.38: Only render links as clickable anchors if the comment author is the site owner (verified safe); other users' links are shown as plain text to prevent spam.
explanations.73: We check for the presence of the 'external' property instead of comparing the `$type` string directly because the type system treats unknown embed types as plain strings, making equality checks unreliable.
explanations.117: Double negation (`!!`) converts the ownerHandle string into a boolean, then we compare it to the comment's author to determine if they're the site owner.
explanations.118: We extract the last segment of the URI (split by `/`) to get the unique record key that identifies this specific post.
explanations.132: Padding increases by 1.5rem for each reply depth level, creating a visual indentation that shows the nesting structure of conversations.
explanations.196: We cast customFields.bluesky to a specific interface type, allowing TypeScript to know what properties are available on the configuration object.
explanations.215: Promise.all runs both the API fetch and blocked-list fetch simultaneously rather than waiting for one to finish before starting the other.
explanations.218: If fetching the blocked list fails (network error, etc.), we catch the error and return an empty Set so the component still renders available comments.
explanations.224: We merge two sources of blocked handles—those hardcoded in the site config and those from the external blocklist—into one Set for efficient lookup.
explanations.229: This recursive function walks the nested reply tree and flattens it into one array, adding a depth number to each comment for indentation rendering.
explanations.235: We skip adding blocked users' comments to the final list, but still recurse through their replies so legitimate responses to them remain visible.
explanations.255: These are the dependencies for the effect—if any of these values change, the effect re-runs to fetch fresh comments.
